study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modeling of brain MRI data identifies small subcortical volumes and associations with cognitive function in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD)

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: CentileBrain used to generate regional volumetric z-scores; specific normative modeling algorithm not specified in this paper.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Individual regional volumetric z-scores were generated using CentileBrain (Ge et al., 2024), an open source online software tool that leverages an aggregated neuroimaging dataset with a large number of individuals (37,407 comparison brains).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional subcortical gray matter volumes (bilateral amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus, accumbens area).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Measurements were obtained for regional subcortical gray matter volumes of the bilateral amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus, and accumbens area

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Normative z-scores adjusted for age, sex, and intracranial volume (ICV).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: A large normative MRI dataset that controlled for sex, age, and intracranial volume was used to quantify the developmental status of 7 bilateral subcortical regional volumes.
